q: The concept of 'thickness' (or Newhouse thickness) of a Cantor set C ⊂ ℝ is defined using the gaps (complementary intervals). A Cantor set C has thickness τ(C) > 0 if the ratio of any 'bridge' (part of C between two gaps at the same level) to the adjacent gap is ≥ τ. Two Cantor sets C₁, C₂ with τ(C₁)·τ(C₂) > 1 must:
exp: Newhouse's gap lemma: if τ(C₁)·τ(C₂) > 1, then C₁ ∩ C₂ ≠ ∅ for any positioning where they interleave. This is used to prove the Newhouse phenomenon: near any diffeomorphism with a homoclinic tangency, there are diffeomorphisms with persistent tangencies (infinitely many attractors).
